item.title: Political violence: How justifications influence voter approval
item.description: What happens when political violence is presented as a justified response to threat or injustice coming from an out-group? A study by Ursula Daxecker, director at the Max Planck Institute for Politics and Social Science in Göttingen, and Neeraj Prasad of the University of Amsterdam, published in The Journal of Politics, finds that legitimizing violence can increase public approval of both violence and the parties involved in it. Among BJP supporters, the effect went even further: when violence was portrayed as justified, they were less approving of a peaceful response by their own party. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Spiny dogfish blood contains a hormone long thought absent in sharks
item.description: Cortisol is a hormone that helps humans and many other animals regulate their energy use and respond to changing conditions. item.title: Finding their sense of direction: Cell movement helps tissues establish polarity
item.description: From the hairs on our arms to the microscopic sensory structures of the inner ear, many tissues in the body are built with a clear sense of direction. To build these structures throughout development, individual cells must establish which way they are facing—and coordinate that orientation with cells around them. If they get this wrong, tissues may fail to form, form improperly or fail to function. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What makes a place ready for radical innovation? Researchers say resident openness matters
item.description: Why do some cities embrace new technologies and business models while others are slower to take them up? Economic conditions, infrastructure and access to technology clearly matter. But a new study from the University of Amsterdam and the University of St Gallen suggests there is another factor that has received much less attention: the psychological openness of the local population. Regions where people are more open to new experiences and unfamiliar ideas are more likely to be early adopters of radical innovations, the study says. Fuente: Phys.org.
